story: Fairbanks votes October 6th and none of the six Assembly candidates told Alaska's News Source they back data centers, with NSF's summer AI awards in Alaska as the runner-up

claims.claim: The Fairbanks North Star Borough regular election is on Tuesday, October 6th.
claims.verbatim: Tuesday, October 6, 2026 Polls Open from 7:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Clerk's Office
claims.notes: Page is undated, so date_of_source is the fetch date. Corroborated by the FNSB sample ballot header 'REGULAR ELECTION - OCTOBER 6, 2026' and by KTUU ('Election Day in Fairbanks is Oct. 6').

claims.claim: Polls are open from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. on election day.
claims.verbatim: Tuesday, October 6, 2026 Polls Open from 7:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m.
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Clerk's Office
claims.notes: Single primary source. Early voting at Noel Wien Library has already ended (the page says it ran from September 21st), so copy should not invite readers to vote early.

claims.claim: The October 6th ballot includes Proposition 3, a citizens' initiative to require hand counting of all ballots and prohibit electronic tabulation.
claims.verbatim: PROPOSITION 3 A CITIZENS' INITIATIVE PROPOSITION REQUIRING ALL BALLOTS TO BE HAND COUNTED BY REGISTERED BOROUGH VOTERS, WITH OBSERVATION AS AUTHORIZED BY LAW, AND PROHIBITING ELECTRONIC TABULATION SYSTEMS
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough (official sample ballot)
claims.notes: Sample ballot PDF is undated, so date_of_source is the fetch date. The ballot also carries Proposition 1 (maximum allowable tax revenues) and Proposition 2 (moving the election to November). The page text says it would 'become effective in 2027'. None of the propositions concern data centers. Also note that the election page summary mentioned a Borough Mayor race, but no mayor race appears on the sample ballot, so do not claim one.

claims.claim: Three Borough Assembly seats are on the ballot, Seats D, E and H, each for a 3-year term.
claims.verbatim: BOROUGH ASSEMBLY SEAT H 3-Year Term (2026-2029) Vote For Not More Than One (1)
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough (official sample ballot)
claims.notes: Matching blocks for SEAT D and SEAT E read identically on the ballot. The Official Candidate List (https://www.fnsb.gov/DocumentCenter/View/28746/Official-Candidate-List-PDF, dated 8/5/2026) lists the same three Assembly seats, each '3-year term'.

claims.claim: Miguel Ramirez and Alexis Howell are the two candidates for Assembly Seat D.
claims.verbatim: BOROUGH ASSEMBLY SEAT D 3-Year Term (2026-2029) Vote For Not More Than One (1) Miguel Ramirez Alexis Howell Write-In
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough (official sample ballot)
claims.notes: Corroborated by the Official Candidate List and KTUU.

claims.claim: Seat D is an open seat because its current holder, Liz Reeves, isn't on the ballot.
claims.verbatim: Alexis Howell, who is running for the open Assembly seat D, agreed with the idea of a moratorium.
claims.notes: Primary corroboration: the FNSB Official Candidate List names 'Liz Reeves' as the individual holding Seat D, and she isn't one of the two candidates. The FNSB Assemblymembers page lists Liz Reeves as Seat D, 'Deputy Presiding Officer'. The URL path says 09/30 but the article is dated September 29th.

claims.claim: Incumbent Nick LaJiness faces Shelly Shupe for Assembly Seat E.
claims.verbatim: Nick LaJiness, running for reelection to seat E, didn't mince words on his opinion on data centers.
claims.notes: Primary corroboration: the sample ballot reads 'BOROUGH ASSEMBLY SEAT E ... Nick LaJiness Shelly Shupe', and the FNSB Assemblymembers page lists Nick LaJiness in Seat E.

claims.claim: Incumbent Scott Crass faces Joshua Leaders for Assembly Seat H.
claims.verbatim: Scott Crass, who is running to retain seat H on the Assembly, defended his vote in favor.
claims.notes: Primary corroboration: the sample ballot reads 'BOROUGH ASSEMBLY SEAT H ... Scott W. Crass Joshua Leaders'. 'His vote in favor' refers to the August 27th vote on the legislative priorities that include the data center moratorium.

claims.claim: Scott Crass is the Assembly's Presiding Officer.
claims.verbatim: Presiding Officer
claims.notes: The title appears on the page next to Scott Crass, Seat H. The page is undated, so date_of_source is the fetch date.

claims.claim: The Fairbanks North Star Borough Assembly has nine members elected at large.
claims.verbatim: The Assembly is composed of nine elected officials. Each member is elected at-large to serve three-year staggered terms.
claims.notes: The page lists nine members, Seats A through I. So three of the nine seats are on the ballot, one third of the body.

claims.claim: The Assembly adopted Resolution 2026-25, identifying its legislative priorities, at its August 27th regular meeting.
claims.verbatim: RESOLUTION NO. 2026-25. A Resolution Identifying And Supporting Legislative Priorities. (Sponsor: Assembly Committee of the Whole) -Adopted
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough Clerk's Office (action memorandum)
claims.notes: Memo dated August 31, 2026, subject 'ACTION OF THE REGULAR ASSEMBLY MEETING OF AUGUST 27, 2026'. It gives no vote tally or roll call. This is background, outside the window.

claims.claim: According to Alaska's News Source, the Assembly voted 6-1 to adopt its 2027 legislative priorities.
claims.verbatim: On Aug. 27, the Assembly voted 6-1 in favor of adopting a set of legislative priorities for 2027.
claims.notes: needs_softening: true. The tally comes from one secondary source only. The primary action memorandum records 'Adopted' with no tally, KUAC's August 31st story gives no tally, and no minutes were found. Who voted no was NOT FOUND. Attribute it as 'voted 6-1, according to Alaska's News Source'. Six for and one against is seven votes from a nine-member body, so two members were apparently absent or didn't vote. Don't assert that either.

claims.claim: Resolution 2026-25 supports a moratorium on permitting, leasing or building new commercial data centers on state-owned or municipal lands in Alaska.
claims.verbatim: The FNSB supports a moratorium on the permitting, leasing, or construction of new commercial data centers on state-owned or municipal lands in Alaska
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough (Resolution No. 2026-25 text)
claims.notes: This is the state priority, lines 111 to 117, titled 'Moratorium on Data Center Development in Alaska'. The fetched copy is the meeting packet version, with the adoption line still blank ('ADOPTED THE _____ DAY OF __________ 2026'). Adoption itself is confirmed by C11. KTUU's paraphrase reads 'municipal or state-owned lands'. The moratorium runs 'until the State of Alaska and local governments have developed and adopted standards', so call it temporary, not a ban.

claims.claim: The moratorium would last until the state and local governments adopt standards on six named impacts, from electrical demand and water to noise and air quality.
claims.verbatim: electrical demand, water consumption and shortages, environmental impacts, noise, air quality, and land use pollution, and other public interest considerations
claims.source_outlet: Fairbanks North Star Borough (Resolution No. 2026-25 text)
claims.notes: The count is six named items plus a catch-all: 1 electrical demand, 2 water consumption and shortages, 3 environmental impacts, 4 noise, 5 air quality, 6 land use pollution, then 'other public interest considerations'. 'Six' is my count of the verbatim list and doesn't appear on the page as a word. If copy uses the number, show the list.

claims.claim: The data center moratorium is the only item that appears in both the state and federal halves of the Assembly's priority list.
claims.verbatim: only one item appears as a priority in both state and federal parts of the list – a request to temporarily halt the development of large commercial data centers in Alaska.
claims.notes: The verbatim keeps KUAC's own dash because it's a quoted source string. Don't carry the dash into slide copy. Primary corroboration: the resolution's federal priority (lines 200 to 206) carries the same title and word-for-word text as the state priority, including 'state-owned or municipal lands'. Background, outside the window.

claims.claim: The Assembly's 2027 legislative priority list totals 25 items across its state and federal sections.
claims.verbatim: The Assembly's list is split between the state and federal levels, totaling 25 priorities.
claims.notes: When I asked for an enumeration of the resolution, one pass listed 21 state and 4 federal items, which sums to 25 and matches KUAC. An earlier pass returned 18 state items. Because the split isn't a verbatim string on the page, the 21 and 4 split is killed as a standalone figure. Use the 25 total, credited to KUAC.

claims.claim: Presiding Officer Scott Crass told KUAC the moratorium request was intended to include federal lands as well.
claims.verbatim: said by phone Sunday that it was intended to include federal lands, as well.
claims.notes: needs_softening: true. This is KUAC's paraphrase of Crass, not his direct quote, so write 'Crass told KUAC it was meant to cover federal land too'. The adopted text itself says only 'state-owned or municipal lands', even in the federal list, and copy must not imply that the text covers federal land. The Air Force parcels are federal land, which is why this point carries weight.

claims.claim: Seat D candidate Alexis Howell agreed with the idea of a moratorium.
claims.verbatim: Alexis Howell, who is running for the open Assembly seat D, agreed with the idea of a moratorium.
claims.notes: KTUU also quotes her as saying 'I think that at the end of the day, a lot more analysis needs to go into that.' That quote was read once, so it's usable but carries lower confidence.

claims.claim: Howell, arguing the borough's grid is already struggling, said "I would hate to see us dump a data center on top of that."
claims.verbatim: Arguing that the borough's grid is currently struggling, Howell said, 'I would hate to see us dump a data center on top of that.'
claims.notes: Matched verbatim in three separate fetches. 'The grid is struggling' is KTUU's paraphrase of Howell's argument and not her words, so keep it outside the quote marks.

claims.claim: Seat D candidate Miguel Ramirez said he can't say "yay" or "nay" because more studies need to be done.
claims.verbatim: but I can't really say 'yay' or 'nay' because I think there need to be more studies done
claims.notes: The fuller passage reads 'I think we should, you know, do a study where we can all agree and see the, work with the environmental folks and find out where the goods are, where the pros are, where the cons are, if it's good, if it's not, but I can't really say...' Quote only the clause above. It was read in one targeted fetch, and its wording was consistent with the scout's report.

claims.claim: Seat E incumbent Nick LaJiness said "I don't think that data centers are good for any community."
claims.verbatim: "I don't think that data centers are good for any community, to be honest with you," LaJinness said.
claims.notes: KTUU misspells the attribution as 'LaJinness'. The ballot and the Assemblymembers page spell it 'LaJiness', so use that spelling in copy. Matched in multiple fetches.

claims.claim: Seat E challenger Shelly Shupe said she is "somewhere in between" those worried about data centers and those who don't want to discount them.
claims.verbatim: "I'm somewhere in between the 'I'm worried about what it might bring' and 'I don't want to discount it' groups," she said.
claims.notes: Matched in two fetches. She is the candidate closest to open-minded, but she doesn't state support.

claims.claim: Seat H incumbent Scott Crass said "Energy costs in our community have skyrocketed."
claims.verbatim: Energy costs in our community have skyrocketed. They're incredibly high, some of the highest in the nation
claims.notes: Matched in three fetches.

claims.claim: Crass called a project that would consume more energy than the entire town "absolutely terrifying at first blush."
claims.value: more energy than our entire town
claims.verbatim: grappling with that while thinking about a project that would consume more energy than our entire town is absolutely terrifying at first blush.
claims.notes: This is Crass's characterization of a hypothetical project. No MW figure is given anywhere in the fetched sources, so don't attach a number to it. Crass defended his vote for the priorities (see C08).

claims.claim: Seat H challenger Joshua Leaders said the impact on infrastructure, the power grid and water needs a serious look to see if the benefit outweighs the cost.
claims.verbatim: We need to take a serious look at the impact on the infrastructure, the power grid, the water and how that's affected, and we need to see if that benefit outweighs the cost
claims.notes: Read in two fetches.

claims.claim: Leaders supports a temporary moratorium while data is collected.
claims.verbatim: Leaders explained, adding that he supports a temporary moratorium while data is collected.
claims.notes: This is KTUU's paraphrase, not a direct quote. Don't put it in quote marks as Leaders' words.

claims.claim: None of the six Assembly candidates quoted by Alaska's News Source expressed outright support for data centers.
claims.value: none of the six (0 of 6 candidates quoted)
claims.verbatim: we need to see if that benefit outweighs the cost
claims.notes: needs_softening: true. This is a claim of absence, so no single string proves it. The verbatim is the most favorable line in the article, from Leaders, and it's conditional. I asked directly whether any candidate expressed outright support and the answer was no. Positions are against (LaJiness), for a moratorium (Howell, Leaders), undecided (Ramirez, Shupe), and defending a pro-moratorium vote (Crass). Required phrasing: 'none of the six told Alaska's News Source they support data centers'. Don't write 'not one says yes' as a bare fact, because it reflects only what one outlet reported and Shupe explicitly doesn't want to 'discount it'.

claims.claim: The Air Force solicitation AFCEC-26-R-0006 seeks lease proposals for AI data centers at JBER, Eielson Air Force Base and Clear Space Force Station.
claims.verbatim: RFLP Artificial Intelligence (AI) Data Center Development at Joint Base Elmendorf Richardson, Eielson Air Force Base, and Clear Space Force Station
claims.notes: Posted April 10th, so this is background. SAM shows a response deadline of May 29th, while HigherGov says it was extended to June 29th. The deadline is disputed between sources and past either way, so don't print it. HigherGov corroborates the title and number. No award appears in either record.

claims.claim: The Pentagon has offered to lease about 4,700 acres of government land in Alaska to private companies for data centers.
claims.verbatim: It's offered to lease about 4,700 acres of government land to private companies, though no projects have been awarded yet.
claims.source_outlet: KUAC via Alaska Public Media (Shelby Herbert)
claims.notes: Independent corroboration from Air and Space Forces Magazine (April 11th): '4,700 acres located across Air Force and Space Force installations in Alaska'. The acreage was not readable on SAM.gov, where it sits in appendices. Background, outside the window.

claims.claim: No data center projects have been awarded under the Air Force leasing offer.
claims.verbatim: though no projects have been awarded yet.
claims.source_outlet: KUAC via Alaska Public Media (Shelby Herbert)
claims.notes: needs_softening: true. This was true as of September 15th. HigherGov (fetched October 2nd) shows the notice past due with no awards recorded, and the SAM API shows no award data. Phrase it as 'no award has been announced' or 'as of mid-September, no projects had been awarded'.

claims.claim: Twelve parcels across the three Alaska installations have been identified for potential data center development.
claims.verbatim: Twelve parcels have been identified for potential development
claims.source_outlet: Air and Space Forces Magazine (Matthew Cox)
claims.notes: Background (April 11th). Alaska Public Media separately reports 'The Pentagon wants to build up to a dozen new military data centers near Anchorage, Healy and Fairbanks', which is consistent. The same article says leases run 'for up to 50 years', but I read that once only. How many of the twelve parcels sit near Eielson was NOT FOUND.

claims.claim: U.S. Senator Lisa Murkowski said she is not a proponent of data centers at JBER or Interior installations because of an insecure energy base.
claims.verbatim: I am not a proponent of data centers down at JBER or at our Interior installations because we are not able to support them because of an insecure energy base at this time,
claims.source_outlet: KUAC via Alaska Public Media (Shelby Herbert)
claims.notes: Matched in two fetches. The article doesn't say when or where she said it, so attribute it to the September 15th KUAC report. Background, outside the window.

claims.claim: Fairbanks already has some of the highest utility costs in the nation, according to KUAC.
claims.verbatim: Fairbanks already has some of the nation's highest utility costs.
claims.source_outlet: KUAC via Alaska Public Media (Shelby Herbert)
claims.notes: Consistent with Crass's 'some of the highest in the nation' (C23). Both are characterizations without a figure. If a number is wanted, use ledger/power_utility.json and not this claim.

claims.claim: Eielson Air Force Base could become the first U.S. military installation powered at least partly by a 5-megawatt microreactor.
claims.verbatim: But if all goes according to plan, the base would be the first U.S. military installation to be powered, at least partly, by a 5-megawatt microreactor.
claims.notes: needs_softening: true. This is a plan, so write 'would' or 'planned'. The page says '5-megawatt' and not 'up to 5 megawatts'. The developer is 'Oklo Inc., the California-based nuclear technology firm that the Defense Logistics Agency Energy has selected'. The site is 'near Spruce Lake, located east of the south end of the main runway'. Dated September 20th, three days before the window, so treat as background.

claims.claim: Public comments on the Eielson microreactor site were due by September 30th.
claims.verbatim: Members of the public can offer comments, but they must be submitted to the Eielson Public Affairs Office no later than Sept. 30.
claims.notes: The comment period has CLOSED as of the run date, so use the past tense. The comments relate to the preferred site's location near wetlands.

claims.claim: The Assembly's next regular meeting after the election is on October 8th.
claims.verbatim: Regular Assembly Meeting
claims.notes: The calendar lists 'Regular Assembly Meeting' on October 8, 2026, 6:00 PM. The verbatim is the entry title. The date comes from the calendar cell, so the string is only weakly bound to it. The calendar doesn't say when newly elected members are seated, so don't claim the winners sit on October 8th.

claims.claim: A second regular Assembly meeting is scheduled for October 22nd.
claims.verbatim: Regular Assembly Meeting
claims.notes: The calendar lists 'Regular Assembly Meeting' on October 22, 2026, 6:00 PM. The same caveat applies as in C36.

claims.claim: Independent U.S. House candidate Bill Hill said he doesn't want data centers to get tax breaks or build vast complexes without local input and support.
claims.verbatim: didn't want to see data centers receive tax breaks or the ability to build vast complexes without local input and support.
claims.notes: This is the Current's paraphrase of Hill. His direct quote is 'The Alaska people are worried about what data centers will do to their lives, and they want assurances.' His independent status and his opponent (Rep. Nick Begich) come from the fetch summary and weren't read verbatim, so verify before printing 'independent'. The claim sentence uses 'Independent' on that basis. Drop the word if it's unconfirmed. In window.

claims.claim: The Fairbanks North Star Borough had an estimated 97,083 residents in 2025.
claims.verbatim: Fairbanks North Star Borough | 97,083
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Labor and Workforce Development
claims.notes: From the 2025 Population Estimates table. The page is undated, so date_of_source is the fetch date. The verbatim is the table row as rendered.

claims.claim: Begich's DATA Act of 2026 would let manufacturers run fully self-contained grid-of-one power systems.
claims.verbatim: fully self-contained, 'grid-of-one' power systems, so innovation can scale without forcing households to subsidize massive new energy demands.
claims.notes: Background (April 21st). needs_softening: true. The press release does NOT mention data centers, so copy must not say the bill targets data centers. Use it only as the other candidate's energy framing, with the bill's own words.

claims.claim: NSF obligated $3,824,575 to the University of Alaska Anchorage for an AI-driven critical mineral recovery project.
claims.verbatim: "fundsObligatedAmt":"3824575"
claims.notes: Award 2614749, 'Collaborative Research: FEC: Transformative Bioprocessing and AI-Driven Frameworks for Sustainable Critical Mineral Recovery'. awardeeName is University of Alaska Anchorage Campus and the PI is Brandon Briggs. It runs from 09/01/2026 to 08/31/2030, and estimatedTotalAmt is also 3824575. I read the amount from the field. My fetch tool reported it unformatted, but its exact JSON quoting wasn't displayed verbatim the way it was for 2614751.

claims.claim: The UAA-led project will combine microbiology and AI to recover rare earth elements from coal mining waste, with UAF, Montana Tech and the University of Wyoming.
claims.verbatim: a use-inspired research initiative led by the University of Alaska Anchorage, in partnership with the University of Alaska Fairbanks, Montana Technological University, and the University of Wyoming, will integrate microbiology and AI to develop scalable biological technologies for domestic REE recovery.
claims.notes: Read from the raw abstractText of award 2614751, which shares its abstract with 2614749. The abstract also says 'AI will predict high-potential materials'. The verbatim runs slightly over 40 words, so trim it for display.

claims.claim: NSF obligated $913,037 to the University of Alaska Fairbanks as the companion award on the critical mineral project.
claims.verbatim: "fundsObligatedAmt":"913037"
claims.notes: Award 2614751, raw JSON read. The PI is Srijan Aggarwal ('pdPIName':'Srijan Aggarwal'). It runs from 09/01/2026 to 08/31/2030, and the funds are recorded as 'FY 2026 = $913,037.00'.

claims.claim: NSF obligated $1,772,170 to the University of Alaska Fairbanks for GAIA, an AI-driven geophysics framework led there by Carl Tape.
claims.verbatim: fundsObligatedAmt: 1772170
claims.notes: Award 2608510, 'Collaborative Research: Frameworks: Geophysical AI-driven Integration & Assimilation (GAIA)'. It runs from 08/01/2026 to 07/31/2032. The verbatim is my fetch tool's rendering of the JSON field, so the value is confirmed but the character-exact quoting isn't.

claims.claim: The GAIA team will test its system on landslides in Alaska and the Pacific Northwest.
claims.verbatim: The investigators test the full system on landslides in Alaska and the Pacific Northwest.
claims.notes: The abstract also says the team 'trains fast surrogate models that approximate expensive physics simulations ... to produce real-time digital twins that forecast geohazards'.

claims.claim: NSF obligated $1,588,147 to the University of Alaska Fairbanks for a fire weather toolkit to advance controlled burning in Alaska.
claims.verbatim: "fundsObligatedAmt":"1588147"
claims.notes: Award 2536745, raw JSON read. The title is 'Collaborative Research: FIRE-WUI: A research-informed fire weather toolkit to advance controlled burning in Alaska' and the PI is Christine F Waigl. It runs from 09/01/2026 to 08/31/2030. AI is listed under 'program'.

claims.claim: The fire weather team will use machine learning on historical weather data to map hazardous fire weather and safe prescribed burn windows across Alaska.
claims.verbatim: Using historical weather reanalysis data and statistical and machine-learning techniques, the research team will characterize the geographic and seasonal patterns of hazardous fire weather
claims.notes: Read from the raw abstractText. The sentence continues 'and identify windows of conditions favorable for safe prescribed burning across Alaska'. Careful, the verbatim contains the banned word 'patterns', which is allowed inside a straight-quoted verbatim but never in copy prose.

claims.claim: NSF awarded $50,000 to the University of Alaska Fairbanks for an I-Corps project on explainable AI that maps underwater depth from satellite imagery.
claims.verbatim: fundsObligatedAmt: 50000
claims.notes: Award 2630206, 'I-Corps: Translation Potential of Explainable Artificial Intelligence (AI) for Satellite-Derived Nearshore Bathymetry and River Profiles'. The PI is Erin Trochim and it runs from 09/01/2026 to 08/31/2027. The abstract phrase is 'explainable artificial intelligence (AI) that converts satellite imagery into high-resolution maps of underwater depth (bathymetry) for coastlines, rivers, and lakes'. The abstract does NOT name Alaska, so don't claim an Alaska purpose for this award. Its only Alaska link is the awardee.

claims.claim: NSF's RAISE award gave the University of Alaska Anchorage $380,000 in 2024 to build rural AI partnerships.
claims.verbatim: "fundsObligatedAmt":"380000"
claims.notes: BACKGROUND, from 2024 and not a summer 2026 award, so don't count it in 'this summer'. Award 2433241, 'Collaborative Research: EPIIC: Rural AI Solutions and Engagement (RAISE)'. The PI is Kenrick Mock and it runs from 08/01/2024 to 07/31/2027. Related background is award 2435188, AI-UNITE, which gave UAA $400,000 (raw '"fundsObligatedAmt":"400000"', dated 09/03/2024).

claims.claim: RAISE created an Alaska AI Solutions Consortium that funds research through a mini-grant program.
claims.verbatim: the creation of an Alaska AI Solutions Consortium that will integrate disparate AI efforts, solicit feedback from the community, and advance research through a mini-grant program
claims.notes: Read from the raw abstractText. The abstract states a plan ('will'), and the UAA pages (N11 to N14) show the mini-grants being carried out.

claims.claim: Full proposals for the 2026-27 RAISE mini-grants are due October 7th.
claims.verbatim: Full Proposal: October 7, 2026
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska Anchorage College of Engineering (AI @ UAA)
claims.notes: The page title is 'RAISE Mini Grants - 2026 Community Partner Call'. The partner statement of need was due September 21, 2026, so it has passed. Awards will be announced on November 2, 2026. Eligible applicants are 'any Alaskan organization outside of the university'. No award amount is stated. The page is undated, so date_of_source is the fetch date.

claims.claim: RAISE will announce its 2026-27 mini-grant awards on November 2nd.
claims.verbatim: Award Announcement: November 2, 2026
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska Anchorage College of Engineering (AI @ UAA)
claims.notes: This is a scheduled date, so write it as 'expected' or 'scheduled'.

claims.claim: The Village of Alakanuk Tribe partnered on a 2025-26 RAISE mini-grant called ARCTIC, AI for rural community transformation and infrastructure coordination.
claims.verbatim: ARCTIC: AI for Rural Community Transformation and Infrastructure Coordination
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska Anchorage College of Engineering (AI @ UAA)
claims.notes: The community partner is listed as 'Village of Alakanuk Tribe' and the faculty PI is Marie E. Lowe. The page summary describes a community planning chatbot and training program, but that description is a paraphrase. The page lists 4 projects in total and no amounts. It's undated, so date_of_source is the fetch date. The 25/26 cycle is background.

claims.claim: Nome Joint Utilities System partnered on a RAISE mini-grant using machine learning to predict the thermal conductivity of warming permafrost.
claims.verbatim: Predicting Thermal Conductivity of Warming Permafrost for Hazards Estimation using Machine Learning
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska Anchorage College of Engineering (AI @ UAA)
claims.notes: The community partner is 'Nome Joint Utilities System' and the faculty PI is Zhaohui (Joey) Yang. The other two projects are an AI parent-training app with Step-In Autism Services and AI media testing with Anchorage partners.

claims.claim: The Fairbanks North Star Borough includes Eielson Air Force Base and Fort Wainwright among its communities.
claims.verbatim: The total population for the Fairbanks North Star Borough, which includes all the communities within the Borough (including Fort Wainwright and Eielson AFB) reached 96,747 for the 2022 calendar year
claims.source_outlet: Military OneSource, U.S. Department of Defense
claims.notes: Fetched by the showrunner after the fact-checker killed the Wikipedia-only version. Page undated, fetch date used. The same page gives the 2025 estimate of 97,083 matching C39.

claims.claim: Eielson Air Force Base is 26 miles southeast of Fairbanks.
claims.verbatim: Eielson AFB is located 26 miles southeast of Fairbanks in the interior of Alaska
claims.source_outlet: Military OneSource, U.S. Department of Defense
claims.notes: Fetched by the showrunner.

claims.claim: Seat H incumbent Scott Crass defended his vote in favor of the legislative priorities.
claims.verbatim: Scott Crass, who is running to retain seat H on the Assembly, defended his vote in favor.
claims.notes: Same verbatim as C08, split out as its own claim by the showrunner so the stance line on slide 02 traces to a claim of its own.

stories_surviving: Fairbanks votes October 6th: six Assembly candidates on data centers, and none told Alaska's News Source they support them
NSF's AI money in Alaska this summer

killed.why: akleg.gov, the BASIS legislature page, Justia's AS 24.05.090 and NCSL all returned 403, and Ballotpedia rendered empty. Not read on any page, so killed. (January 19th, 2027 is the third Tuesday, so the claim is plausible, but plausible isn't verified.)

killed.claim: Resolution 2026-25 lists 21 state and 4 federal priorities.
killed.why: No verbatim count exists on the page. Two passes over the same document disagreed (18 state on one, 21 state on the other). Use KUAC's verbatim '25 priorities' total (C16) instead.

killed.claim: Named Assemblymember(s) voted no in the 6-1 vote.
killed.why: The roll call wasn't found. The primary action memorandum records only 'Adopted', KUAC gives no tally, and no minutes were reachable.

killed.claim: Eielson Air Force Base lies within the Fairbanks North Star Borough.
killed.why: The only source reached was Wikipedia (both the Eielson and FNSB articles, which come from the same publisher and aren't independent). The Air Force page returned 403 and Census Reporter returned the wrong place. No primary or second independent source, so killed under the single-source rule. Copy may say Eielson is 'near Fairbanks' only if another claim supports it.

killed.claim: North Pole Middle School is X miles from an Eielson-area data center parcel.
killed.why: Not in the Alaska Public Media September 15th article, and no other source was found.

killed.claim: N of the twelve parcels are near Eielson.
killed.why: No parcel count per base appears in any fetched source. SAM.gov refers to Appendices A-1 to A-3, which weren't readable.
